summary: Policy propagation staleness leads to console-runtime routing mismatch for SLA macros
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-02-28 09:12 UTC, several internal support tickets were observed where the Redwood Console preview for SLA-macro-based routing did not match the routing decision recorded in the serving runtime. Impact: approximately 5-10% of support routing decisions in us-east were evaluated differently by the runtime than what the Console UI and rule editor showed, causing misclassification of SLA cohorts and delayed escalations. Environment: prod us-east, routing-engine v3.4.2, propagation-service v2.9, console-api v1.15.2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create or edit a macro that applies cohort weighting and time-window rules. 2) Save in Console and use "Preview routing" for sample token ids. 3) Issue a test request with the same token ids to the runtime trace endpoint and compare executed route. 4) Observe mismatch in ~1 out of 10 cases when updates occur within a short window after prior edits. Observations and logs: routing-propagation queue shows message reorder and duplicate delivery in traces (link to logs below). Slack thread: #support-runtime-propagation. Initial CI/PR that touched propagation commit: routing-service commit 9d3f1b0.
comments: 2026-03-01 10:04 - Support (Aisha Patel): Noticed multiple customer-facing tickets where Console preview said SLA=gold but runtime routed to SLA=silver. Pinging SRE to validate propagation path.

2026-03-01 11:30 - SRE (Marco Liu): Reproduced with a local runloop against prod snapshots. Observed propagation delays of 30-90s in some messages and at least one message redelivery that overwrote a newer policy (message ordering bug).
2026-03-02 09:15 - Product (Evelyn Gomez): Are we certain this is ordering-only? Could template merge logic in the console be producing stale caches?
2026-03-03 14:22 - Eng (Sandeep Rao): Added temporary feature flag to enable strict-version-check on propagation consumer. Will test traffic in us-east canary tomorrow.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: propagation-service uses at-least-once delivery with tombstone messages; race between tombstone and update can revert a newer policy.
Hypothesis B: console-api caches macro templates and returns preview based on cache TTL while propagation pushes new JSON into queue — cache invalidation gap.
Telemetry: added a paired-hash check: console_preview_hash vs runtime_active_hash per trace id. Initial run shows 7% divergence over 6 hours.
Logs: routing-propagation queue consumer logs show consumer instance id rs-prop-3 experienced GC pause ~2026-02-28T09:05:18Z causing re-queue and duplicate apply of older sequence number.
Related PR: routing-service PR #1289 addresses ordered-apply by persisting sequence id with monotonic increments and guarding against out-of-order applies.
resolution_notes: Mitigation deployed 2026-03-02 02:00 UTC: Enabled strict-version-check flag on propagation consumer to reject out-of-order sequence numbers. This reduced mismatch rate in canary to <0.5%.
Hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/1289. The hotfix adds durable sequence persistence and idempotent apply logic.
Short-term workaround: support ops instructed to wait 90s after macro edits before running bulk changes and to use the 'force-propagate' button when making immediate SLA-critical edits.
Rollout plan: staged rollout to all us-east propagation consumers 2026-03-05 03:00 UTC, followed by metric sweep for 48h. If stable, promote to eu-west next week.
Customer impact remediation: backfilled misrouted tickets identified between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-01; CS notified affected customers and adjusted escalations where needed.
next_steps: Complete full rollout and monitor paired-hash divergence metric until stable below 0.2% for 24h.
Add automated test to release pipeline that simulates rapid macro edits and validates propagation ordering across retention windows.
Improve Console cache invalidation logic to invalidate on successful write and expose propagation lag in UI for operators.
Postmortem: document root cause and timeline in Confluence and link incident to page; schedule blameless review with SRE and Product.
